claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game is prone to crashes, bugs, and technical issues requiring patches or workarounds.

citations.review_text:
I played Oblivion for the first time last year when I purchased the Remastered version on launch day...it was a bad enough experience with the optimization issues that I put it down in the early game and thought I'd never play Oblivion again. Recently, I remembered that I purchased the Game of the Year Edition on Steam from a sale long ago and thought I'd give it a try, since I enjoyed the Remastered version when it was playable. I can wholeheartedly say that Oblivion never needed a remaster, because the original game is not only still very playable, but also an excellent RPG that hearkens back to some of the best days of the genre. I love that I can enjoy Oblivion without constant lagging, screen tearing, crashing and more issues that still plague the remaster. Spell crafting is innovative and provides a lot of flexibility for different build ideas, which Skyrim sorely lacks.

A lot of Oblivion GOTY Edition doesn't look great, especially the faces and general mechanics of NPCs. I imagine that there are plenty of mods to improve these flaws of the game. Overall, it's a blast from the past for new and old players alike. I'd definitely forego the remaster and play this version of Oblivion instead.

You get the intended vision, it's far cheaper, you don't need a monster PC to run it, and there's no weird woke censorship.  Male and Female character selection, not "Body Type 1 and 2".

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the quests, factions, and expansions like The Shivering Isles as major highlights.

citations.review_text: The atmosphere is really great, and the quests too.

Truly the best rpg from that time, people really like to glazing Skyrim but i think Oblivion is just better in some aspects especially writing wise, the dark brotherhood questline is one of the coolest there imo, cant wait to try The Shivering Isle.

This game is such a step up from Morrowind in every way. Horses and instant fast travel from anywhere dials up the pace so you don't spend 20 minutes walking to objectives over and over again, streamlined and intuitive menus hasten preparation and encounters, and widespread voice acting makes the world feel more alive than ever. Plus the game doesn't crash every time you switch windows anymore.

Each of the factions are a joy to play through, particularly the Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isle expansions which are one of those rare cases of DLC perhaps being even better than the original game. Even the base quest lines like the Mages guild and Dark Brotherhood are still also so much fun.

I really love this game. The setting, Cyrodiil, feels so warm and inviting. Like home. Some people recommend Skyrim as a game everyone should play at least once but I think it's Oblivion. The perfect culmination of what makes Western RPGs so great.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the leveling system as unorthodox and punishing for players going in blind without prior research.

citations.review_text:
7.5/10, daddy Todd <3. 

Honestly, what an incredible game. I feel if I was to sit here and type out everything I loved about this game I could write whole novels; instead, I shall say the ONE major thing that screwed me up for about 3 or 4 hours of gameplay, that being the levelling system. I went into this game blind and treated it how I did Skyrim. Oh boy was that stupid. This game uses such a weird levelling system that honestly you should 100% look into it before playing however, if you do it right (or play on a lower difficulty) you shouldn't face much issue.

Asides from that, I love this game and honestly cannot wait to get right back into with the dlc and other playthroughs.

Oblivion is still an absolute joy to this day, despite the fact the levelling system may come across as unorthodox there's an almost limitless amount of roleplaying, questing and spell making to do here. The game is casual enough to be approached by even RPG newcomers but deep enough to allow for a significant amount of roleplaying, with tons of places guilds and dungeons to explore. The dungeons are a bit samey but the DLC and experience more than make up for a few lackluster elements, anyone who is looking to get into RPG games or scratch that exploration and immersion itch this is an excellent middle ground between the hardcore Morrowind and rather casual Skyrim.

I'm sure there's mods or whatever to reduce this, but I didn't bother.

Second, like with a lot of Bethesda DLC, the DLC are just overpowering and I wanna deactivate them. Overshadows the whole game.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that buying potions can be very expensive, making alchemy a necessary and helpful skill to learn.

citations.review_text: I played Morrowind and now I'm playing Oblivion.  I played it years ago and have problems with the leveling system.  A friend helped me understand that you don't necessarily want to work on the main quest right away.  With that knowledge this playthrough has been much more enjoyable.  I did much of the fighters and mage guild quests.  Then went on to do the main quest. Things went much better. I also learned how to do Alchemy and that makes things doable because buying potions is really expensive in this game.

Good game once you learn the mechanics, unfortunately the game doesn't tell you much, or even misleads you. The Old Knight's guides were helpful.

Melee and magic are more fun than in TES5, but archery feels slightly worse. Physical weapon damage is too low but magic integrates well into any build to compensate. Being able to cast a spell even while holding a two-handed weapon is amazing. Equipment degrades a bit too quickly but I like durability as a mechanic.

The UI and hotkeys/shortcuts are awful, especially coming from SkyUI. This and the tiny map were my biggest peeves while playing. Not being able to put an arrow back in your quiver and having to shoot it at the ground isn't fun, but you get used to it.

The writing is generally good, and the world is fun to explore.

Graphics are fine, I wish more modern games would use low-res graphics like TES4/5, and focus on good game mechanics and writing, unfortunately we are seeing a trend in the opposite direction with modern games, so my faith in TES6 is not too high.

I realized I never rated this game, so here I am
I have about 400 hours on steam, but I played more than that a long time ago (around 2008 I guess)
This game is fire. 
It has this sweet spot between the complexity and interesting quests of morrowind and the enjoyable gameplay (including fights) of skyrim. It still leaves you the ability to create your own spells (to break the game if you want).

I replayed it a few months ago with [b]Maskar's Oblivion Overhaul[/b], making the fights more enjoyable and the game more challenging overall, you can even build your own house wherever you want with it. it was amazing. 

The only thing I don't like much is the fact that you have to min max your character a bit if you don't want the enemies becoming (much) stronger than you as you level up, but this can be fixed with mods (eg: oblivion XP, set XP gained to X5 and don't train)
I especially recommend the dark brotherhood questline. Back when I was a teenager, I thought it was so cool. Now I think the voice acting of Lucien Lachance is hilarious. In both cases it was a blast.
I 100% recommend it.

claims.claim: The game features native PC controls that can be difficult to use with a controller without community controller maps.

citations.review_text: The controls are entirely for PC unfortunately, but if you're able to find a community controller map that works well enough for you, then it's just plain ol' Oblivion.

Honestly in spite of the memes, this really has been my favorite game of all time. It was my first experience with the Elder Scrolls series, and I enjoyed playing for a few years as a kid before I realized there was a main quest after Kvatch. Then in anticipation of Skyrim, I discovered there was, and I fell in love all over again, and I bought the Shivering Isles disc. The PS3 version only had that to expand with as the Knights of the Nine, so that was the most I could do. 

I always managed to come back to it, somehow, whether it was moving onto XBox 360 or finally Steam, I always loved Oblivion. 

Then, mystically, just before the remaster comes out, I play the creation club add-ons for Skyrim that feature the music from oblivion, right before the remaster. Then it shadowdrops, and I was happy as I could be. I got to fall in love with Cyrodiil again.

This game was more of the depth of my later childhood than Pokémon could ever claim. It was my first real, personal exposure to the fantasy genre, and I love it dearly still. If you feel the need to play the original instead of the remaster, give it a try in spite of any controller compatibility. It’s worth it.

citations.review_text: Absolute classic, which still looks great 20 years after release. With mods graphics can be quite on pair with modern games and if installed properly, very stable. Gameplay-wise if you aim to have perfectly leveling character it is quite a challenge. For those who like to exercise theyr brain cells.
Crappy world scaling aside it's an awesome game, fully worth the money even without the additional dlcs. Do yourself a favor and install the unofficial patches though.

claims.claim: Reviewers report experiencing game-breaking bugs that permanently break save files and require console commands to finish the game.

citations.review_text:
What a ride it has been. This game truly touches me every time I come back to it. I’ve grown so attached to the characters, and the music completely pulls me in every time. There’s something about the atmosphere that makes this game feel like a world that’s somehow my own, and it’s hard to explain just how special that feeling is.

I tried to finish this one a while back, but ever since Cloud Ruler Temple I ran into a game-breaking bug that left my save permanently broken, with things like falling through the map continuing all the way to the end. After a lot of messing around with the console, I eventually managed to finish it. Despite all that, I’d still take this version, with all its quirks and drama, over the remaster any day.

A truly great game that I’ll never forget, and hopefully one I’ll return to someday.

Oblivion remains one of the greatest open-world RPGs ever made. The Game of the Year Edition bundles the base game with Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isles, delivering an enormous, beautifully detailed world packed with freedom, memorable quests, deep character progression, and endless exploration.
Strengths:

Expansive, immersive Cyrodiil full of Radiant AI NPCs, epic storylines, and side content that can consume hundreds of hours.
Excellent combat, magic, stealth, and build variety.
Stunning (for its time) graphics, atmospheric soundtrack, and strong voice acting (including Patrick Stewart).

Weaknesses:

Infamous bugs and jank (levelling quirks, repetitive dungeons, occasional glitches). <install the unoffical patch>
Some dated mechanics and loading times.

Even years later, it's a generational masterpiece that rewards creativity and curiosity. The GOTY version makes it the definitive way to experience this beloved classic.
Final Score: 9.5/10 — Still worth playing in 2026.
